done_when: forge sync sets the roadmap and spotted-list merge rule to run the installed Forge (the forge command on PATH, through a forge hook subcommand), never a checkout path, so any worktree's sync leaves a rule that keeps working after that worktree is removed. New repos get it at init; existing repos get it from their next forge sync or forge doctor --fix. One command-level test: sync in a worktree, remove it, and a spotted-list merge in another worktree still merges by itself.

findings.body: A repo adopted with v1.2.2 has only the roadmap merge attribute: that release's src/forge/sync.py registers ROADMAP_RULE alone. After upgrading, doctor --fix installs the new driver but leaves .gitattributes unchanged; src/forge/doctor.py:200–201 only reports generated-file drift, while src/forge/sync.py:269–272 supplies the missing spotted-list attribute through sync. Spotted-list merges therefore still conflict when this existing repo upgrades through doctor --fix alone, contrary to Done-when. The doctor test masks this by running current-release sync first at tests/test_merge_rule_survives_worktree_removal.py:59. Ensure doctor registers both paths and test the previous-release upgrade without that preparatory sync.
findings.title: Not done: doctor --fix enables spotted-list merging in repos adopted on the previous release

findings.body: When repo is forge-source and core.hooksPath is unset, checks_hooks deliberately excludes the default commit and push hooks. Driver drift now enters this repair branch anyway and calls install_shims, which unconditionally writes both hooks before updating the driver (src/forge/sync.py:409–426; src/forge/githooks.py:53–55). Thus doctor --fix unexpectedly enables shared commit and push gates across all source worktrees while reporting only a merge-rule repair. Repair the driver without installing hooks when checks_hooks is false.
findings.title: Preserve the source-repo hook exclusion during driver repair

why: forge sync points git's merge rule for the roadmap and spotted list at the checkout that ran it, so after running sync in a work folder, merges use that folder's old code (or a deleted folder) and the spotted list conflicts
